title: Physics task development of prospective physics teachers using ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT 3.5 can support the development of physics assessment tasks by prospective teachers, compared with a traditional textbook-based approach. The central question is not student learning, but the quality of the tasks prospective teachers create and how they revise them after receiving either AI-generated prompts or textbook examples.

The study used a randomized controlled trial with 26 prospective physics teachers from Ludwig-Maximilians-University Munich. Participants were divided into an intervention group that used ChatGPT 3.5 and a control group that used a high-school physics textbook. All participants created four text-based conceptual tasks for 10th-grade high school physics, focused on kinematics and Newton’s laws. The intervention group also completed a usability and perceived usefulness survey about ChatGPT.

Results showed that ChatGPT-supported and textbook-supported groups produced similarly correct tasks and tasks of comparable overall quality, but the textbook group produced clearer tasks and more often embedded them in meaningful context. Both groups struggled most with task specificity, meaning they often omitted information needed to solve the tasks. ChatGPT was rated as easy to use, but its output quality was judged only neutral to slightly poor. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support prospective physics teachers, but prompt design and teacher training are still needed to improve the pedagogical quality of the tasks produced.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s conversational large language model chatbot for generating and revising text based on prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as a support tool by prospective physics teacher students to generate four conceptual physics assessment tasks for 10th-grade German high school students, compared with a textbook condition.

findings.finding_summary: In a randomized controlled trial with n=26 prospective physics teachers, task correctness did not differ significantly between ChatGPT and textbook conditions. However, ChatGPT tasks scored lower on clarity (p=0.04, d=0.38) and context (p=6�b710^-5, d=1.04), while specificity, misleading phrasing, and adequacy of difficulty showed no significant differences.
findings.measure: Task quality ratings: specificity, clarity, correctness, misleading phrasing, adequate difficulty, context, relevance to target concept, overall quality

findings.finding_summary: Participants rated ChatGPT usability highly (mean 4.1/5) but judged its output quality as slightly below neutral (mean 2.76/5) and perceived usefulness as neutral (mean 3.24/5). Response time was not viewed as a major barrier (mean 2.09/5 for the slowdown item).
findings.measure: System Usability Scale, Technology Acceptance Model 2 items on perceived usefulness and output quality

quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized controlled trial with a small sample and clear comparison condition, using direct task-quality ratings and usability measures. There are some concerns about small n and single-site sampling, but the design is experimental and credible.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a medium-to-large positive effect for context quality in favor of the textbook and a small effect for clarity, with no difference on correctness. Overall impact is modest and mixed rather than strongly positive.
